newsitem.title: USA: California insurance chief certifies quake unit.
newsitem.headline: California insurance chief certifies quake unit.

text.p: California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush cleared the way Tuesday for the California Earthquake Authority (CEA) to begin selling insurance policies on December 2, a spokesman said.

Quackenbush spokesman Richard Wiebe said the commissioner certified that insurance companies representing over 70 percent of the state's residential property insurance market had signed agreements to participate in the authority.

Wiebe said the commissioner also certified that the Internal Revenue Service had determined that the CEA was exempt from federal income taxation and that commitments had been obtained from reinsurers in the required amount.
"There's nothing standing in the way of the CEA selling policies beginning on Monday, December 2," Wiebe said.

Greg Butler, the CEA's interim chief executive officer, said earlier that the authority had secured the backing of 71.6 percent of California's residential insurance market, just over the 70 percent required.
Insurance companies representing at least 70 percent of the California residential insurance market had to agree to participate in the earthquake authority for the authority to become operational.
"We are on target to begin operations on Monday," Butler said.
